_comment: D-G2: the board's address decides the tracker. ONE table, two readers -- Tests/Test-Setup.ps1 runs Scripts/Resolve-Tracker.ps1 over it, Tests/test_tracker.py runs agent/core/config.py's tracker(). org is orgs[].org as configured. Rows that carry `owner` also pin the owner rule (Get-P20TrackerOwner / tracker_owner): the address's first path segment, case preserved. If the two halves ever disagree about a row, one of them is wrong.

rows.why: a blank address is a local board: no tracker, no owner
the shipped placeholder is ADO-SHAPED; whether it is contacted is the tier's business, not this rule's
the legacy Azure DevOps address -- its org lives in the HOST, so the owner rule answers nothing
a GitHub owner: the second tracker
a repo-grained GitHub address is still GitHub, and still names its owner; owner-or-repo grain is the spec's open item, not this rule's
case and the www prefix do not change the host, and the owner keeps its case -- it is a display name too
a pasted address without a scheme still names the host and the owner
a port does not change the host
an unknown host keeps today's behavior -- every address meant ADO before this rule; a third tracker changes this row ON PURPOSE, here first
GitHub Enterprise is the spec's open item; until it is designed, an unknown host is ADO like any other
